canonical_name: Stoer-Wagner deterministic global minimum-cut algorithm family
literal_source_claim_zh: 全局最小割的确定性算法
literal_source_claim_en: A deterministic algorithm for the global minimum cut.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies an algorithm name and purpose but no truth-valued proposition. It fixes no graph representation, weight domain, cut and output semantics, maximum-adjacency-search state or tie policy, contraction and provenance model, termination clause, correctness conjunction, complexity model, ordered binders, hypotheses, conclusion, or boundary cases. The inspected primary source identifies the mathematical route but the catalog does not decide whether the root is phase correctness, contraction recurrence, end-to-end partial or total correctness, witness production, runtime, or a conjunction. Selecting one would invent proposition-changing mathematics before independent source admission and review.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted target must fix a finite vertex carrier, ordinary simple versus weighted multigraph representation, edge/capacity object, weight carrier and order/addition structure, cut and partition carrier, supervertex/contraction representation, algorithm-state and output types, cost carrier, universes, and every typeclass and decidability assumption.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose the contraction recurrence, maximum-adjacency phase lemma, end-to-end partial correctness, total correctness and termination, a returned minimum weight, a witnessing original-vertex partition, the source runtime bound, or an exact conjunction.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; every graph, weight, cut, search, contraction, tie, output, termination, provenance, and cost boundary in scope-map.md remains for the statement phase.
candidate_scope_not_credited: Theorem 2.1's comparison between a minimum s-t cut and the minimum cut after merging s and t
Lemma 3.1's maximum-adjacency phase cut as a minimum s-t cut
end-to-end correctness of repeated phases and contractions returning the lightest phase cut
termination and production of a minimum-cut witness on the original vertex set
the O(|V||E| + |V|^2 log |V|) running-time theorem under the source implementation model
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty and singleton vertex types, where no nontrivial cut exists
two vertices, empty or disconnected graphs, isolated vertices, and zero minimum-cut weight
zero-weight and negative-weight edges and exact versus approximate weights
parallel edges and self-loops before and after contraction
tied maximum-adjacency keys, arbitrary starting vertices, and deterministic tie policies
multiple minimum cuts and witness versus weight-only output
lifting phase cuts through nested supervertices to the original vertex type
the last one- or two-supervertex phase and termination boundary
arithmetic and priority-queue cost, overflow, and floating-point behavior if complexity or executability is included
excluded_substitutions: a directed maximum-flow/minimum-cut or fixed-source s-t cut theorem
unweighted SimpleGraph edge connectivity without the selected weights, cut semantics, algorithm, and checked bridge
a convenient special graph class, fixed weight domain, fixed search order, or unique-minimum assumption not present in the approved root
a structure or premise storing the desired cut or correctness result
a finite example, benchmark, floating-point experiment, oracle, or unchecked certificate
the untrusted verified label or the discovery-only Lean probe
